question:
Which of the following idioms given in the alternatives has the meaning?

"To become discouraged and give up hope."
option_2: To wear one's heart on one's sleeve
option_3: To have a heart of gold
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. To lose heart.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "to lose heart" means to become discouraged and to give up hope, especially after a setback. (हिम्मत हार जाना)
◦ Example: He did not lose heart even after failing the examination twice.

 

• All four options are built on the word "heart", and the question therefore tests the candidate's ability to distinguish between idioms drawn from the same word-family — a pattern that recurs constantly in SSC papers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: To take heart (साहस बटोरना): To gain courage or confidence — the direct opposite of losing heart.

 

• Option 2: To wear one's heart on one's sleeve (भावनाएँ खुलकर प्रकट करना): To show one's feelings openly instead of concealing them.

 

• Option 3: To have a heart of gold (उदार हृदय होना): To be extremely kind and generous by nature.

 

NOTE

 

• Other idioms built on "heart": "To have one's heart in one's mouth" (to be terrified), "To have a change of heart" (to alter one's opinion), "By heart" (from memory), "To pour out one's heart" and "A heart of stone" (to be unfeeling).

 

• Related idioms of discouragement: "To throw in the towel", "To give up the ghost" and "To be down in the dumps".

question:
Which of the following idioms given in the alternatives has the meaning?

"To watch somebody or something carefully."
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. To keep an eye on.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "to keep an eye on" means to watch somebody or something carefully, either to guard it or to make sure that nothing goes wrong. (निगरानी रखना)
◦ Example: Please keep an eye on my luggage while I buy the tickets.

 

• The four options are all "eye" idioms with quite distinct meanings, and the question turns on distinguishing them.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: To turn a blind eye (जानबूझकर अनदेखा करना): To pretend not to notice something wrong — very nearly the opposite of keeping an eye on it.

 

• Option 2: To have an eye for (पारखी दृष्टि होना): To have good judgement or taste in a particular matter — *She has an eye for detail.*

 

• Option 3: To see eye to eye (सहमत होना): To agree completely with somebody.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "eye" idioms often tested: "To keep an eye out for" (to look out for), "An eye for an eye" (retaliation in kind), "In the twinkling of an eye" (instantly), "To catch one's eye" (to attract attention) and "The apple of one's eye" (a cherished person).

 

• Note the difference between "to keep an eye on" (to watch over) and "to keep an eye out for" (to be on the lookout for something expected).

question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct meaning of the idiom.

"Once in a blue moon."
option_4: Only during the hours of night
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Very rarely, hardly ever.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "once in a blue moon" means very rarely; hardly ever. (कभी-कभार / बहुत कम)
◦ Example: Since he moved abroad, he visits his old school once in a blue moon.

 

• A "blue moon" is the name given to a second full moon occurring within the same calendar month, which happens only about once in two and a half years. The rarity of the event gave the idiom its meaning.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 is the exact opposite, and would be expressed by "day in and day out" or "without fail".

 

• Option 2 describes regularity, for which one would say "like clockwork" or "at regular intervals".

 

• Option 4 takes the word "moon" literally and confines the idiom to night-time.

 

NOTE

 

• Other idioms of frequency and time: "Every now and then" (occasionally), "Off and on" (intermittently), "In the nick of time" (just in time), "At the eleventh hour" (at the last possible moment), "Till the cows come home" (for a very long, indefinite period) and "Donkey's years" (a very long time).

question: Choose the correctly spelt word from the given options.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Definitely.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct spelling is "Definitely" — without any doubt; certainly. (निश्चित रूप से)
◦ Example: He will definitely attend the meeting tomorrow.

 

• Spelling key: the word is built on "finite" — DE + FINITE + LY. If the candidate remembers that *definite* contains *finite*, the temptation to write "definately" disappears at once.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "Definately" — incorrect; "a" has been written in place of the "i" of *finite*. This is by far the commonest misspelling in English.

 

• Option 2: "Defenitely" — incorrect; "e" has been written in place of the first "i".

 

• Option 3: "Definitly" — incorrect; the "e" before "-ly" has been dropped.

 

NOTE

 

• Related words: definite, definitely, definition, indefinite and definitive (conclusive and authoritative).

 

• Other adverbs frequently misspelt: separately, immediately, occasionally, necessarily, sincerely, truly (note: no "e"), argument (no "e") and judgement/judgment (both accepted, the first being the usual British form).

question: Choose the correctly spelt word from the given options.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Separate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct spelling is "Separate" — forming a unit by itself; to divide or set apart. (अलग / पृथक करना)
◦ Example: The two departments were housed in separate buildings.

 

• Spelling key: there is "a rat" in separate — SEP-A-RATE. This is the standard mnemonic and settles the question at once, since the commonest error is to write an "e" in place of the middle "a".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "Seperate" — incorrect; "e" has been written in place of the middle "a". This is among the most frequently misspelt words in the language.

 

• Option 2: "Saperate" — incorrect; the first "e" has been replaced by "a".

 

• Option 3: "Sepatate" — incorrect; "t" has been written in place of the "r".

 

NOTE

 

• Related forms: separation, separately, separatist and inseparable — all retaining the "a".

 

• Other words with a commonly mistaken vowel: grammar (not grammer), calendar (not calender), existence (not existance), maintenance (not maintainance) and privilege (not priviledge).

question:
Select the option with the correct spelling that can replace the underlined word in the given sentence. If the spelling in the given sentence is already correct, choose Option 4 "No replacement required".

His unpresidented rise within the department surprised all his colleagues.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. unprecedented.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The word in the sentence, "unpresidented", is misspelt. The correct spelling is "unprecedented". (अभूतपूर्व / अप्रत्याशित)

 

• "Unprecedented" means never having happened before; without any earlier example.
◦ Example: The scheme drew an unprecedented response from applicants.

 

• Spelling key: the word is built on "precedent" — UN + PRECEDENT + ED. A *precedent* is an earlier instance, so what has no precedent is *unprecedented*. The error arises because the word is often confused in sound with "president".

 

• The corrected sentence reads: *His unprecedented rise within the department surprised all his colleagues.*

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "unpresedented" — incorrect; the "c" of *precedent* has been replaced by "s".

 

• Option 3: "unprecidented" — incorrect; "i" has been written in place of the second "e".

 

• Option 4 is incorrect because the given word is misspelt and does require replacement.

 

NOTE

 

• Related words from the same root: precede (to come before), precedent (an earlier instance serving as a rule), precedence (priority in rank) and antecedent.

 

• Do not confuse precede (to go before) with proceed (to go forward) — a pair very frequently tested in SSC papers.

question:
Choose the correct synonym of the bold word in the following sentence.

The chairman gave a lucid explanation of the new policy to the shareholders.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Clear.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Lucid" means expressed clearly and easy to understand. (सुस्पष्ट / सुबोध)
◦ Example: The professor is admired for his lucid style of teaching.

 

• The word comes from the Latin *lucidus*, meaning bright or shining — the same root that gives lucent, translucent and elucidate.

 

• In the sentence, an explanation given to shareholders would naturally be praised for being clear, which confirms the choice.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Confusing (भ्रामक): The exact antonym of lucid.

 

• Option 3: Lengthy (लंबा): Concerns the length of the explanation, not its clarity.

 

• Option 4: Hasty (जल्दबाज़ी में किया गया): Done in a hurry — again irrelevant to clarity.

 

NOTE

 

• Synonyms of lucid: Clear, Intelligible, Coherent, Perspicuous, Plain, Comprehensible.

 

• Antonyms: Obscure, Vague, Ambiguous, Muddled, Abstruse, Unintelligible.

 

• Note the second, medical sense: a "lucid interval" is a period of clear thinking between spells of confusion or unconsciousness. The verb elucidate means to make something clear by explaining it.

question:
Match the word with its closest synonym.

Word: Obstinate
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Stubborn.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Obstinate" means stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion or course of action, in spite of persuasion or good reason. (हठी / जिद्दी)
◦ Example: He was too obstinate to admit that he had made a mistake.

 

• "Stubborn" carries exactly this sense and is therefore the closest synonym.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Flexible (लचीला): Willing to change or compromise — an antonym of obstinate.

 

• Option 2: Agreeable (सहमत होने वाला): Willing to agree, or pleasant in manner — also opposite in sense.

 

• Option 3: Obedient (आज्ञाकारी): Willing to comply with orders — again an antonym.

 

NOTE

 

• Synonyms of obstinate: Stubborn, Headstrong, Adamant, Intransigent, Obdurate, Recalcitrant, Wilful, Dogged.

 

• Antonyms: Compliant, Amenable, Docile, Tractable, Yielding, Accommodating.

 

• Note the shade of difference: persistent and determined are usually terms of praise, while obstinate, stubborn and pig-headed carry disapproval, though all describe an unwillingness to give way.

question:
Select the correct alternative to fill in the blank with the correct preposition in the following sentence.

The management did not object ______ the proposal put forward by the workers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. to.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The verb "object" is followed by the preposition "to", meaning to express disapproval of or opposition to something. (आपत्ति करना)
◦ Example: Nobody objected to the change in the timetable.

 

• The completed sentence reads: *The management did not object to the proposal put forward by the workers.*

 

• Note also that "object to" is followed by a noun or a gerund, never by an infinitive — *I object to being treated in this manner*, not "to be treated".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "on" is used with "insist on", "depend on", "comment on" and "congratulate on".

 

• Option 3: "for" is used with "apologise for", "blame for", "account for" and "long for".

 

• Option 4: "against" is used with "protest against", "warn against" and "guard against". It is the sharpest distractor here, because *protest against* and *object to* are close in meaning but take different prepositions.

 

NOTE

 

• Verbs regularly followed by "to": object to, respond to, refer to, react to, listen to, belong to, adhere to, consent to, submit to, yield to, attend to, subscribe to and look forward to.

 

• Remember that in "object to", "look forward to" and "be accustomed to", the word "to" is a preposition and must be followed by a gerund.

question: Choose the word that is most opposite in meaning to "hostile".
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Friendly.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Hostile" means unfriendly, showing strong opposition or dislike; of or belonging to an enemy. (शत्रुतापूर्ण / विरोधी)
◦ Example: The proposal met with a hostile reception from the members.

 

• "Friendly" means kind and pleasant; behaving as a friend, and is therefore the correct antonym. (मैत्रीपूर्ण)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Antagonistic (विरोधी): Showing active opposition — a synonym of hostile.

 

• Option 2: Belligerent (युद्धप्रिय / झगड़ालू): Eager to fight or quarrel — also a synonym.

 

• Option 3: Aggressive (आक्रामक): Ready to attack or confront — again close in sense.

 

NOTE

 

• Synonyms of hostile: Inimical, Adversarial, Unfriendly, Malevolent, Combative.

 

• Antonyms: Amicable, Cordial, Genial, Hospitable, Sympathetic, Congenial.

 

• Note the useful pair "hostile takeover" in business and "hostile witness" in law, both of which retain the sense of opposition.

question: Choose the word that is the antonym of "Take off" (as used of an aircraft).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Land.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The phrasal verb "take off", used of an aircraft, means to leave the ground and begin to fly. (उड़ान भरना)
◦ Example: The flight took off half an hour behind schedule.

 

• Its antonym is "land", which means to come down to the ground after a flight. (उतरना)
◦ Example: The aircraft landed safely in spite of the poor visibility.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Ascend (ऊपर चढ़ना): To go up — a synonym of the upward movement in "take off".

 

• Option 3: Depart (प्रस्थान करना): To leave — close in sense to taking off, and not its opposite.

 

• Option 4: Rise (उठना): To move upward — again a synonym.

 

NOTE

 

• "Take off" has several other meanings, each with its own opposite:
◦ To remove a garment — *take off your coat*; opposite: put on
◦ To become suddenly successful — *the business really took off*
◦ To imitate somebody in mockery — the noun is a take-off
◦ To take time away from work — *to take a day off*

 

• Other phrasal verbs with opposite pairs: switch on / switch off, pick up / put down, get on / get off, turn up / turn down and build up / break down.

question: Choose the word that is the antonym of "Surplus".
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Deficit.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Surplus" means an amount that remains over and above what is required or used; an excess. (अधिशेष / बचत)
◦ Example: The state reported a revenue surplus for the third year running.

 

• "Deficit" means the amount by which something falls short of what is required; a shortfall, and is therefore the correct antonym. (घाटा / कमी)
◦ Example: The budget showed a fiscal deficit of three per cent of GDP.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Excess (अधिकता): An amount beyond what is necessary — a synonym of surplus.

 

• Option 2: Abundance (प्रचुरता): A very large quantity — again close in sense.

 

• Option 4: Overflow (अतिप्रवाह): A flowing over of what cannot be contained — also a synonym in the figurative sense.

 

NOTE

 

• The pair is important in economics, where it is constantly tested:
◦ Budget surplus / Budget deficit — receipts exceeding or falling short of expenditure
◦ Trade surplus / Trade deficit — exports exceeding or falling short of imports
◦ Fiscal deficit — the excess of total expenditure over total receipts excluding borrowings
◦ Revenue deficit — the excess of revenue expenditure over revenue receipts

 

• Synonyms of deficit: Shortfall, Shortage, Insufficiency, Arrears, Loss.

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A government ruled by a small privileged group of people.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Oligarchy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An "oligarchy" is a form of government in which power rests with a small group of privileged persons, whether distinguished by wealth, birth, military strength or family connection. (कुलीनतंत्र / अल्पतंत्र)
◦ Example: The republic gradually decayed into an oligarchy of a few landed families.

 

• The word comes from the Greek *oligos* (few) and *arkhein* (to rule).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Democracy (लोकतंत्र): Government by the people, exercised directly or through elected representatives.

 

• Option 3: Autocracy (निरंकुश तंत्र): Government by a single person with absolute power.

 

• Option 4: Bureaucracy (नौकरशाही): Government by officials rather than by elected representatives.

 

NOTE

 

• Forms of government frequently asked as one-word substitutions:
◦ Monarchy — rule by a king or queen
◦ Aristocracy — rule by the nobility
◦ Plutocracy — rule by the wealthy
◦ Theocracy — rule by religious authority in the name of God
◦ Meritocracy — rule by those selected on merit
◦ Gerontocracy — rule by the elderly
◦ Matriarchy / Patriarchy — rule by women / by men
◦ Anarchy — the absence of government altogether

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A government ruled by religious leaders in the name of God.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Theocracy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A "theocracy" is a system of government in which priests or religious leaders rule in the name of God, and in which religious law is the law of the state. (धर्मतंत्र)
◦ Example: The country was governed for a time as a theocracy, with the clergy exercising final authority.

 

• The word comes from the Greek *theos* (god) and *kratos* (rule).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Monarchy (राजतंत्र): Government by a king or queen, who may rule absolutely or, as in a constitutional monarchy, reign without governing.

 

• Option 3: Meritocracy (योग्यतातंत्र): A system in which advancement is based on ability and achievement rather than on wealth or birth.

 

• Option 4: Anarchy (अराजकता): The absence of government and of any recognised authority; hence, disorder.

 

NOTE

 

• India is declared a sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic by the Preamble of the Constitution. The words "socialist" and "secular" were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.

 

• Secularism, as understood in India, means that the State has no religion of its own and treats all religions equally — the opposite of a theocracy.

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A large group of people or vehicles travelling together, especially across a desert.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Caravan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A "caravan" is a group of travellers, traders or pilgrims journeying together, especially across a desert or through dangerous country, often with pack animals. (कारवाँ / यात्री दल)
◦ Example: The caravan halted at the oasis before crossing the last stretch of desert.

 

• The word is of Persian origin, from *karwan*. The resting places built along such routes were called caravanserais or sarais, many of which were built in India by Sher Shah Suri along the Grand Trunk Road.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Entourage (अनुचर वर्ग): A group of attendants who accompany an important or famous person. The emphasis is on attendance upon somebody, not on travel across country.

 

• Option 3: Convoy (काफिला): A group of vehicles or ships travelling together under armed escort for protection.

 

• Option 4: Fleet (बेड़ा): A group of ships sailing together, or the whole body of ships of a navy or company.

 

NOTE

 

• Collective terms frequently asked in SSC: a flock of sheep or birds, a herd of cattle, a swarm of bees, a shoal of fish, a pride of lions, a pack of wolves, a troop of monkeys, a galaxy of stars, a bunch of keys, a bouquet of flowers, a fleet of ships and a horde of savages.

question:
Select the correct alternative to fill in the blank with the correct preposition in the following sentence.

The committee has been asked to look ______ the complaint within a fortnight.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. into.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The phrasal verb "look into" means to investigate or examine a matter carefully. (जाँच करना)
◦ Example: The police have promised to look into the matter without delay.

 

• The completed sentence reads: *The committee has been asked to look into the complaint within a fortnight.* Since a complaint is something to be investigated, only "look into" fits.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "look after" (देखभाल करना): To take care of somebody or something — *She looks after her ageing parents.*

 

• Option 3: "look over" (सरसरी दृष्टि डालना): To examine quickly or casually. Note the contrast with "look into", which implies a thorough inquiry, and with "overlook", which means to fail to notice.

 

• Option 4: "look for" (खोजना): To search for something — *He is looking for his spectacles.*

 

NOTE

 

• Other phrasal verbs with "look": look up (to consult a dictionary, or to improve), look up to (to respect), look down upon (to despise), look forward to (to anticipate with pleasure), look out (to be careful), look on (to watch without taking part) and look through (to examine, or to ignore somebody deliberately).

question:
In the given question, a sentence is divided into four parts and given in the alternatives 1, 2, 3 and 4. There is an error in one part. Choose the alternative containing that part of the sentence that has the error.

The doctor advised him/ to abstain from/ smoking and/ to refrain of alcohol.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. to refrain of alcohol.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The error lies in the preposition. The verb "refrain" is always followed by "from", never by "of".
◦ Correct: *to refrain from alcohol*
◦ Incorrect: *to refrain of alcohol*

 

• The corrected sentence reads: *The doctor advised him to abstain from smoking and to refrain from alcohol.*

 

• Note that both abstain and refrain take "from", which makes the error in the fourth part all the more conspicuous when set beside the correct usage in the second.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "The doctor advised him" is correct — "advise" is properly followed by an object and then an infinitive.

 

• Option 2: "to abstain from" is correct — abstain always takes "from".

 

• Option 3: "smoking and" is correct — a gerund must follow the preposition "from".

 

NOTE

 

• Verbs regularly followed by "from": refrain from, abstain from, prevent from, prohibit from, desist from, differ from, recover from, suffer from, borrow from, derive from and protect from.

 

• A related distinction often tested: one is protected from danger, deprived of a right, accused of an offence and charged with a crime.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1. The tailor's shop had stood at the corner of the lane for forty years.

A. Customers came less for the stitching than for the conversation.

B. He worked at a treadle machine that his father had bought secondhand.

C. Above it hung a calendar from a year that nobody could now remember.

D. Both machine and calendar outlasted three generations of fashion.

S2. When the shutters finally came down, the lane felt oddly quiet in the evenings.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. BCDA.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct sequence is S1 – B – C – D – A – S2, moving from the machine → the calendar above it → both together → the shop's real attraction.

 

• S1 → B: S1 introduces the shop. B takes us inside it and introduces the treadle machine, the first object of the description.

 

• B → C: C begins "Above it hung a calendar", and the pronoun "it" refers to the machine of B. This makes B-C a mandatory pair in that order.

 

• C → D: D speaks of "Both machine and calendar", which can only be said after both have been introduced — in B and C respectively.

 

• D → A: A turns from the objects to the people, and states what really drew customers to the shop. It prepares the way for S2.

 

• A → S2: S2 records the closing of the shop and the quiet that followed, which follows naturally from the mention of conversation in A.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (CBDA) is incorrect because C begins with "Above it", and the pronoun has no antecedent until the machine is named in B.

 

• Option 3 (BCAD) is incorrect because D refers to "both machine and calendar" and must follow immediately upon their description, not after the digression in A.

 

• Option 4 (CBAD) is incorrect on both counts.

 

NOTE

 

• The phrase "Both X and Y" is one of the most reliable clues in para-jumbles: the sentence containing it must come after both X and Y have been separately introduced.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1. Nobody in the office knew what the locked cupboard contained.

A. The peon said it had been locked since long before his own time.

B. Some said old files; others, a broken typewriter.

C. When the new officer finally had it opened, it held neither.

D. Inside were forty tins of biscuits, sealed and untouched.

S2. Nobody could explain them, and nobody was willing to throw them away.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. BACD.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct sequence is S1 – B – A – C – D – S2, moving from speculation → the oldest testimony → the opening → the discovery.

 

• S1 → B: S1 states that nobody knew what the cupboard held. B gives the guesses people made — old files, or a broken typewriter. Speculation follows naturally upon ignorance.

 

• B → A: A adds the peon's testimony, that it had been locked since long before his own time, which explains why nobody knew and deepens the mystery.

 

• A → C: C brings the turning point — the new officer has the cupboard opened — and reports that it held "neither", a word that refers back to the two guesses made in B.

 

• C → D: D reveals what it actually held — forty tins of biscuits. This must follow the statement that it held neither of the expected things.

 

• D → S2: S2 says nobody could explain "them", the pronoun referring to the tins of D.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (ABCD) is incorrect because C says the cupboard held "neither", which requires the two guesses of B to have been stated already — and here B comes after A but the reference still works; the stronger objection is that speculation (B) flows directly from S1's statement of ignorance.

 

• Option 3 (BCAD) is incorrect because A, the peon's account of the long-locked cupboard, cannot come after it has already been opened in C.

 

• Option 4 (ABDC) is incorrect because D discloses the contents before C has told us that the cupboard was opened at all.

 

NOTE

 

• The word "neither" in C is the decisive clue. It refers to exactly two things, and those two things are named only in B — so B must precede C, and D must follow it.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1. The seed library began with a single steel almirah in a school storeroom.

A. Farmers who borrowed a variety were asked to return twice the quantity after the harvest.

B. A retired teacher had collected forty varieties of rice from the villages nearby.

C. Within six years the almirah had become four, and the varieties three hundred.

D. In this way the collection grew without any money ever changing hands.

S2. None of it was ever bought, and none of it was ever sold.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. BADC.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct sequence is S1 – B – A – D – C – S2, moving from the origin → the method → the principle behind it → the result.

 

• S1 → B: S1 introduces the seed library and its single almirah. B explains how it began — a retired teacher had collected forty varieties of rice from nearby villages.

 

• B → A: A describes the method of working — borrowers returned twice the quantity after the harvest. This is the arrangement that made the collection grow.

 

• A → D: D begins with "In this way", which refers directly to the arrangement described in A, and states the principle: the collection grew without any money changing hands.

 

• D → C: C gives the result in figures — within six years, four almirahs and three hundred varieties.

 

• C → S2: S2 closes by restating the principle of D in a memorable form: none of it was ever bought or sold.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (BDAC) is incorrect because D begins with "In this way", which must refer back to a method already described — and that method is given only in A.

 

• Option 2 (ABDC) is incorrect because A speaks of farmers borrowing "a variety", which presupposes that the collection of varieties has already been introduced in B.

 

• Option 4 (ABCD) is incorrect for the same reason, and it also separates D from the arrangement it explains.

 

NOTE

 

• Phrases such as "In this way", "By this means", "Thus" and "As a result" are backward-looking connectives: the sentence containing them must always follow the sentence describing the method or cause.

question:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the question based on the passage.

 

Relativism is the view that truth, value and morality are not absolute but depend upon the standpoint from which they are judged — the culture, the historical period or the individual concerned. It gained ground in the modern period partly through anthropology, which showed that practices condemned in one society were honoured in another, and partly through a growing suspicion of any single tradition that claimed to speak for all mankind.
Two forces have carried it further in our own time. The first is the ease of contact between societies, which places rival systems of belief side by side and makes the claims of each look local rather than universal. The second is a fragmentation within societies themselves, so that even neighbours may no longer share a common frame of reference. In such conditions the relativist position seems less a philosophical doctrine than a plain description of experience.
Its critics raise an objection that has never been fully answered. If every standard is valid only within its own framework, then the relativist's own principle is valid only within his — and he has no ground on which to recommend it to anybody else. A doctrine that undermines the possibility of argument cannot itself be argued for.
The practical consequences are more mixed than either side admits. Relativism has fostered tolerance, and has made people slower to condemn what they do not understand. But it has also made some of them slower to condemn what they ought to, since a settled conviction that all judgements are equally local leaves no clear ground for objecting to cruelty.

 

According to the passage, what is the central claim of relativism?
option_1: That truth and morality are eternal and unchanging
option_2: That truth, value and morality depend upon the standpoint from which they are judged
option_3: That only statements verified by science can be regarded as true
option_4: That every society ought to adopt one common code of morality
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. That truth, value and morality depend upon the standpoint from which they are judged.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The passage opens with the definition: *"Relativism is the view that truth, value and morality are not absolute but depend upon the standpoint from which they are judged — the culture, the historical period or the individual concerned."*

 

• Three standpoints are named — culture, historical period and individual — and the doctrine holds that a judgement can be made only from within one of them, never from outside all of them.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 states the opposite position, that of absolutism, which relativism denies.

 

• Option 3 describes positivism, a different doctrine altogether, which the passage does not discuss.

 

• Option 4 is contrary to relativism, which denies that any single code can claim authority over all societies.

 

NOTE

 

• In passages that open by defining a concept, the first sentence almost always contains the answer to any question about the central claim. Read it closely before considering the options.

• Option 3 draws a practical recommendation that the passage nowhere offers.

question: In the context of Indian planning, what is meant by the term 'Plan Holiday'?
option_1: A period in which planning was handed over entirely to the private sector
option_2: A year in which no government expenditure was incurred at all
option_3: A break given to planners between two Five Year Plans
option_4: A period in which planning was suspended and three Annual Plans were adopted
solution_text:
The correct answer is A period in which planning was suspended and three Annual Plans were adopted.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The term "Plan Holiday" refers to the period from 1966 to 1969, when the Five Year Plans were suspended and three Annual Plans were adopted in their place. (योजना अवकाश — 1966 से 1969)

 

• The reasons for the suspension were the failure of the Third Five Year Plan (1961-66), which had been wrecked by:
◦ The Sino-Indian War of 1962 and the Indo-Pak War of 1965
◦ A severe drought and famine in 1965-66
◦ The devaluation of the rupee in 1966 and a serious shortage of foreign exchange

 

• During the Plan Holiday, priority was given to agriculture, and the Green Revolution was launched with high-yielding varieties, chemical fertilisers and assured irrigation.

 

• The Fourth Five Year Plan began only in 1969.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other interruptions in Indian planning: the Rolling Plan (1978-1980) introduced by the Janata Government in place of the Fifth Plan, and the two Annual Plans of 1990-92, caused by political instability and the economic crisis.

 

• The Second Five Year Plan sought to give the State the "commanding heights of the economy", that is, control of the vital and basic industries.

 

• The Planning Commission, set up in 1950, was replaced by NITI Aayog on 1 January 2015. The Twelfth Plan (2012-17) was the last Five Year Plan.

 

NOTE

 

• The three remaining alternatives are invented explanations. The term has nothing to do with a break given to planners, a suspension of government expenditure, or any handing over of planning to the private sector; it denotes only the substitution of Annual Plans for a Five Year Plan between 1966 and 1969.

question: The Kadambas of Banavasi were the earliest indigenous ruling dynasty of which present-day Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kadambas of Banavasi were the earliest indigenous ruling dynasty of the region that is now Karnataka. Their capital, Banavasi, lies in the present Uttara Kannada district. (कदंब वंश — बनवासी, कर्नाटक)

 

• The dynasty was founded in about 345 CE by Mayurasharma (Mayuravarma), a Brahmana student who is said to have taken up arms after being insulted at Kanchi, and who carved out a kingdom from Pallava territory.

 

• The Kadambas were the first dynasty to use Kannada as an administrative language. The Halmidi inscription of the fifth century, the earliest known Kannada inscription, belongs to their period.

 

• Kakusthavarma was the greatest ruler of the line. The dynasty was eventually absorbed by the Chalukyas of Badami.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other early dynasties of the Deccan and the south:
◦ Satavahanas — the earliest great Deccan power, with their capital at Pratishthana (Paithan)
◦ Chalukyas of Badami — founded by Pulakeshin I; famous for the temples at Aihole, Badami and Pattadakal
◦ Rashtrakutas — founded by Dantidurga; builders of the Kailasa Temple at Ellora
◦ Pallavas of Kanchi — founded as a major power by Simhavishnu; builders of Mahabalipuram
◦ Cholas — the imperial line founded by Vijayalaya, with their capital at Thanjavur
◦ Gangas of Talakad — another early Karnataka dynasty, contemporaries of the Kadambas

 

NOTE

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 2): The land of the Cholas, Pandyas and Pallavas.

 

• Kerala (Option 3): Ruled in early times by the Cheras.

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 4): Associated with the Satavahanas, the Ikshvakus and later the Kakatiyas.

question: Which Mughal emperor finally annexed the Sultanate of Ahmadnagar to the empire?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shah Jahan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sultanate of Ahmadnagar was finally annexed by Shah Jahan in 1636, when the last claimant was captured and the kingdom extinguished. (अहमदनगर का अंतिम विलय — शाहजहाँ, 1636)

 

• The struggle had been long. Akbar attacked Ahmadnagar in 1595, where it was defended with great courage by Chand Bibi, and captured the fort in 1600; but the kingdom survived under Malik Ambar, the remarkable Abyssinian minister who resisted the Mughals for years by guerrilla warfare and reorganised the revenue system on the model of Todar Mal.

 

• After Malik Ambar's death in 1626 the kingdom weakened rapidly, and Shah Jahan completed its annexation. Bijapur and Golconda were later annexed by Aurangzeb, in 1686 and 1687 respectively.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The five Deccan Sultanates, which emerged from the break-up of the Bahmani kingdom, were:
◦ Nizam Shahis of Ahmadnagar
◦ Adil Shahis of Bijapur
◦ Qutb Shahis of Golconda
◦ Imad Shahis of Berar
◦ Barid Shahis of Bidar

 

• Their combined forces defeated the Vijayanagara Empire at the Battle of Talikota in 1565.

 

• Aurangzeb spent the last twenty-five years of his reign in the Deccan, and his prolonged campaigns there are regarded as a principal cause of the decline of the Mughal Empire.

 

NOTE

 

• Akbar (Option 1): Captured the fort of Ahmadnagar in 1600, but the kingdom continued to exist.

 

• Jahangir (Option 2): Fought Malik Ambar repeatedly without success.

 

• Aurangzeb (Option 4): Annexed Bijapur (1686) and Golconda (1687), not Ahmadnagar.

question: Which Veda is recited by the Adhvaryu priest and deals chiefly with the procedure of sacrifices?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Yajurveda.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Yajurveda deals chiefly with the rituals and procedures of sacrifice, and is recited by the Adhvaryu priest, who performs the physical acts of the sacrifice. (यजुर्वेद — अध्वर्यु पुरोहित, यज्ञ की विधि)

 

• It is partly in prose and partly in verse, and is the only Veda to contain prose passages. It has two branches — the Shukla (White) Yajurveda, which keeps the mantras and the prose commentary separate, and the Krishna (Black) Yajurveda, in which they are mixed.

 

• The four Vedas and their priests:
◦ Rigveda — the oldest Veda; 1,028 hymns in 10 mandalas; recited by the Hotri priest
◦ Samaveda — the Veda of melodies, the root of Indian music; sung by the Udgatri priest
◦ Yajurveda — the Veda of sacrificial formulae; recited by the Adhvaryu
◦ Atharvaveda — the latest Veda; charms, spells and remedies; associated with the Brahma priest

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Vedas are called Shruti — that which is heard — and are held to be apaurusheya, not of human authorship. Each Veda has four parts: Samhita, Brahmana, Aranyaka and Upanishad.

 

• The Gayatri Mantra, addressed to Savitri, occurs in Mandala III of the Rigveda; the Purusha Sukta, describing the origin of the four varnas, occurs in Mandala X.

 

• The Upanishads are also called Vedanta. The motto "Satyameva Jayate" is taken from the Mundaka Upanishad.

 

NOTE

 

• Rigveda (Option 1): The oldest Veda, a collection of hymns of praise.

 

• Samaveda (Option 2): The Veda of music and melody.

 

• Atharvaveda (Option 4): The Veda of magical charms and spells, and a valuable source for the beliefs of ordinary people.

question: Which cell organelle is known as the 'powerhouse of the cell'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mitochondria.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The mitochondrion is called the "powerhouse of the cell", because it is the site of cellular respiration, in which energy is released from food and stored as ATP (adenosine triphosphate) — the energy currency of the cell. (माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया — कोशिका का ऊर्जा गृह)

 

• Mitochondria have a double membrane; the inner membrane is deeply folded into structures called cristae, which greatly increase the surface area available for the reactions of respiration.

 

• They possess their own DNA and ribosomes, and are therefore able to make some of their own proteins — a fact that supports the theory that they were once independent organisms. Mitochondrial DNA is inherited from the mother alone.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Cell organelles and their popular names:
◦ Ribosome — the "protein factory" of the cell; found free in the cytoplasm and attached to the rough endoplasmic reticulum
◦ Lysosome — the "suicide bag"; contains digestive enzymes and destroys worn-out organelles
◦ Golgi apparatus — the "traffic police" or dispatching unit; packages and directs materials
◦ Chloroplast — the "kitchen" of the plant cell, where photosynthesis occurs
◦ Nucleus — the "control room" or brain of the cell
◦ Vacuole — the storage sac, very large in plant cells

 

• The cell was discovered by Robert Hooke in 1665; Leeuwenhoek first saw living cells; and the cell theory was propounded by Schleiden and Schwann.

 

NOTE

 

• Ribosome (Option 1): The site of protein synthesis, not of energy release.

 

• Lysosome (Option 2): Contains hydrolytic enzymes and carries out intracellular digestion.

 

• Golgi apparatus (Option 3): Packages and secretes materials.

question: According to Megasthenes, Mauryan society was divided into how many classes?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Seven.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Megasthenes, in his account "Indica", recorded that Mauryan society was divided into seven classes. (मेगस्थनीज — सात वर्ग)

 

• The seven classes he named were: philosophers, farmers, soldiers, herdsmen, artisans, magistrates and councillors.

 

• His account is notable for making no mention of the four varnas or of untouchability, and modern historians therefore treat his division as a classification by occupation rather than by caste.

 

• Megasthenes was the ambassador of Seleucus Nicator at the court of Chandragupta Maurya at Pataliputra. His original work is lost, and survives only in quotations by later Greek writers such as Strabo, Arrian and Diodorus.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Megasthenes also described the municipal administration of Pataliputra, which he said was carried on by six committees of five members each — thirty members in all — dealing with industry, the care of foreigners, births and deaths, trade and commerce, the manufacture and sale of goods, and the collection of the sales tax.

 

• He described the city as being defended by a wooden palisade with 64 gates and 570 towers, and called it "Palibothra".

 

• Other sources for Mauryan history: Kautilya's Arthashastra, the Ashokan edicts, Vishakhadatta's Mudrarakshasa and the Buddhist chronicles Dipavamsa and Mahavamsa.

 

NOTE

 

• Four (Option 1) is the number of varnas in the traditional Brahmanical scheme — a classification Megasthenes does not use.

 

• Five (Option 2) is the number of members in each committee of the Pataliputra municipality, and Six (Option 3) the number of such committees — figures frequently confused with the number of classes.

question: 'Rouf' is a traditional folk dance of which of the following Indian regions?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jammu & Kashmir.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rouf (Rauf) is a traditional folk dance of the Kashmir valley, performed chiefly by women. (रऊफ — जम्मू और कश्मीर)

 

• It is danced in two facing rows, the women linking arms and moving forward and backward with a distinctive footwork called the chakri step. It is performed especially during spring and at Eid, and also at weddings.

 

• Other folk dances of Jammu & Kashmir: Kud, Dumhal (performed by the men of the Wattal tribe), Bhand Pather (folk theatre), Bacha Nagma and Hafiza. The best-known folk music forms are Chakri, Sufiana Kalam and Wanawan, the last sung at weddings.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Folk dances of the northern states, frequently asked in SSC:
◦ Himachal Pradesh — Nati (recognised by the Guinness Book as the largest folk dance), Chohara, Dangi, Kinnauri
◦ Punjab — Bhangra (men), Giddha (women), Jhumar, Sammi, Kikli
◦ Uttarakhand — Chholiya, Barada Nati, Jhora, Langvir
◦ Haryana — Khoria, Ghoomar, Loor, Phag
◦ Rajasthan — Ghoomar, Kalbelia, Chari, Bhavai, Terah Taali

 

NOTE

 

• Himachal Pradesh (Option 2): Known for Nati and Chohara.

 

• Punjab (Option 3): Known for Bhangra and Giddha.

 

• Uttarakhand (Option 4): Known for Chholiya, a sword dance performed at weddings.

question: 'Bagurumba', popularly known as the butterfly dance, is performed by which community?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Bodos of Assam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bagurumba is the traditional folk dance of the Bodo community of Assam, and is popularly called the "butterfly dance" because of the graceful, fluttering movements of the dancers' outstretched arms and colourful garments. (बागुरुम्बा — असम के बोडो समुदाय का नृत्य)

 

• It is performed by women during the Bwisagu festival, the Bodo new year celebrated in the month of Bohag (April), and is accompanied by instruments such as the kham (a long drum), the sifung (a bamboo flute), the jotha and the serja.

 

• The movements imitate those of butterflies, birds and the wind through the trees, and the dance is regarded as an expression of the community's closeness to nature.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Folk dances of the North-East and the communities that perform them:
◦ Assam — Bihu (the state's best-known dance), Bagurumba (Bodo), Jhumur (tea tribes), Ojapali
◦ Meghalaya — Nongkrem and Shad Suk Mynsiem (Khasi), Wangala (Garo), Laho (Jaintia)
◦ Mizoram — Cheraw, the bamboo dance, and Khuallam
◦ Nagaland — Chang Lo and Zeliang; the Hornbill Festival showcases all the tribes
◦ Manipur — Thabal Chongba, Lai Haraoba, Thang Ta
◦ Tripura — Hojagiri, performed balancing on earthen pitchers

 

• Bodo is one of the 22 scheduled languages and belongs to the Sino-Tibetan family; it is written in the Devanagari script.

 

NOTE

 

• The Khasis (Option 2): Perform the Nongkrem and Shad Suk Mynsiem dances of Meghalaya.

 

• The Mizos (Option 3): Perform Cheraw, the bamboo dance.

 

• The Angamis (Option 4): A Naga tribe, known for the Sekrenyi festival.

question: The 'Mopin' festival is celebrated by which tribe of Arunachal Pradesh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Galo.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mopin is the principal festival of the Galo tribe of Arunachal Pradesh, celebrated in April to mark the harvest and to invoke the goddess Mopin Ane for prosperity, good health and a rich crop. (मोपिन — गालो जनजाति, अरुणाचल प्रदेश)

 

• Its distinctive feature is the smearing of rice flour on the faces of participants, which is regarded as a mark of purity and good fortune. The Popir dance is performed by young women, and the rice beer apong is distributed.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Major festivals of Arunachal Pradesh and their tribes:
◦ Mopin — Galo
◦ Solung — Adi
◦ Dree — Apatani, an agricultural festival
◦ Nyokum — Nyishi, the largest tribe of the state
◦ Losar — Monpa, who follow Tibetan Buddhism
◦ Boori Boot — Hill Miri; Reh — Idu Mishmi; Sangken — Khampti and Singpho

 

• Arunachal Pradesh became a full state in 1987, is the largest of the North-Eastern states by area, and is called the "Land of the Rising Sun" and the "Orchid State of India". Its capital is Itanagar, and the Tawang Monastery is the largest in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Apatani (Option 2): Celebrate the Dree festival; their terraced paddy-cum-fish cultivation in the Ziro valley is on the UNESCO tentative list.

 

• Nyishi (Option 3): The most populous tribe of the state; they celebrate Nyokum.

 

• Monpa (Option 4): A Buddhist tribe of the Tawang region; they celebrate Losar and Torgya.

question: The 'Hola Mohalla' festival, begun by Guru Gobind Singh, is celebrated chiefly in which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Punjab.

• Hola Mohalla is celebrated chiefly at Anandpur Sahib in Punjab, and was begun by the tenth Sikh Guru, Guru Gobind Singh, in 1701. (होला मोहल्ला — आनंदपुर साहिब, पंजाब)

 

• It falls on the day after Holi, in the month of Chet, and was instituted as an occasion for the Sikhs to display their martial skills. The Guru intended it as a contrast to the merely festive character of Holi, and as training for a community that had to be ready to defend itself.

 

• The festival features displays of Gatka, the Sikh martial art, mock battles, horsemanship by the Nihangs, and processions, followed by kirtan and the langar.

 

• Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa at Anandpur Sahib on Baisakhi in 1699, and instituted the five Ks.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Regional forms of Holi across India, frequently asked in SSC:
◦ Lathmar Holi — Barsana and Nandgaon, Uttar Pradesh
◦ Baithki Holi and Khadi Holi — Kumaon, Uttarakhand
◦ Shigmo — Goa; Rang Panchami — Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh
◦ Yaosang — Manipur; Dol Jatra / Basanta Utsav — West Bengal
◦ Phagwah — Bihar; Bhagoria — Jhabua, Madhya Pradesh
◦ Hola Mohalla — Punjab

 

• Other festivals of Punjab: Baisakhi, Lohri, Teej, Maghi and the Jor Mela.

 

NOTE

 

• Haryana (Option 2): Celebrates Teej, Gugga Naumi and the Surajkund Crafts Mela.

 

• Himachal Pradesh (Option 3): Celebrates Kullu Dussehra and the Minjar Fair.

question: As per the Census of India, a person who works for 183 days or more in a year is classified as a ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Main worker.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India, a Main Worker is a person who works for 183 days (six months) or more during the reference year. (मुख्य श्रमिक — वर्ष में 183 दिन या अधिक कार्य)

 

• A Marginal Worker is one who works for less than 183 days in the year. Together, main and marginal workers constitute the total workers; everyone else is a non-worker.

 

• The Census classifies workers into four categories by occupation:
◦ Cultivators
◦ Agricultural labourers
◦ Workers in household industry
◦ Other workers

 

• The Work Participation Rate is the percentage of total workers to the total population. In Census 2011 it was about 39.8%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• As per Census 2011, roughly 54.6% of the total workforce was engaged in the primary sector, although that sector contributes a far smaller share of Gross Value Added — an instance of disguised unemployment.

 

• Types of unemployment frequently asked: disguised (more workers than needed), seasonal (common in agriculture), structural, frictional, cyclical and educated unemployment.

 

• Employment data are also collected through the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), conducted by the National Statistical Office since 2017-18.

 

NOTE

 

• Marginal worker (Option 2): Works for less than 183 days in the year — the exact counterpart of the main worker.

 

• Cultivator (Option 3): A category of worker classified by occupation, not by the number of days worked.

 

• Non-worker (Option 4): A person who did not work at all during the reference period, such as students, homemakers and dependants.

question: Under the Regulating Act of 1773, the Supreme Court was established at Calcutta in which year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1774.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Supreme Court at Calcutta was established in 1774 under the provisions of the Regulating Act of 1773. (कलकत्ता में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय — 1774)

 

• It consisted of a Chief Justice and three other judges, the first Chief Justice being Sir Elijah Impey. Its jurisdiction extended over British subjects in Bengal, Bihar and Odisha.

 

• The Regulating Act of 1773 was the first step by the British Parliament to regulate the affairs of the East India Company. Its main provisions were:
◦ It designated the Governor of Bengal as the Governor-General of Bengal, with an Executive Council of four members; Warren Hastings was the first
◦ It made the Governors of Bombay and Madras subordinate to the Governor-General of Bengal
◦ It provided for a Supreme Court at Calcutta
◦ It prohibited the servants of the Company from engaging in private trade or accepting presents

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Later constitutional landmarks:
◦ Pitt's India Act, 1784 — established a Board of Control, creating the system of dual government
◦ Charter Act, 1813 — ended the Company's trade monopoly except in tea and trade with China
◦ Charter Act, 1833 — made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India; Lord William Bentinck was the first
◦ Charter Act, 1853 — introduced open competition for the civil services
◦ Government of India Act, 1858 — transferred power from the Company to the Crown

 

NOTE

 

• 1773 (Option 1): The year the Regulating Act itself was passed, one year before the Court was set up — the commonest confusion in this question.

 

• 1781 (Option 3): The year of the Amending Act, which resolved the conflict between the Supreme Court and the Governor-General in Council.

 

• 1784 (Option 4): The year of Pitt's India Act.

question: Who founded the reform association called the 'Prarthana Samaj' in 1867?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Atmaram Pandurang.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Prarthana Samaj was founded at Bombay in 1867 by Dr. Atmaram Pandurang, with the encouragement of Keshab Chandra Sen, who visited western India in that year. (प्रार्थना समाज — आत्माराम पांडुरंग, 1867)

 

• It was in effect the western Indian counterpart of the Brahmo Samaj, and worked for social reform more than for theological argument. Its four-point programme was:
◦ The abolition of caste distinctions
◦ Widow remarriage
◦ Women's education
◦ Raising the age of marriage for both boys and girls

 

• Its most distinguished members were Mahadev Govind Ranade, who became its guiding spirit, and R.G. Bhandarkar. Ranade also founded the Widow Remarriage Association and the Deccan Education Society.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Reform movements and their founders, frequently asked together:
◦ Brahmo Samaj (1828) — Raja Rammohan Roy, the Father of the Indian Renaissance
◦ Arya Samaj (1875) — Swami Dayanand Saraswati; slogan "Back to the Vedas"
◦ Prarthana Samaj (1867) — Atmaram Pandurang
◦ Ramakrishna Mission (1897) — Swami Vivekananda
◦ Satyashodhak Samaj (1873) — Jyotiba Phule
◦ Theosophical Society (1875) — Madame Blavatsky and Colonel Olcott
◦ Aligarh Movement — Sir Syed Ahmad Khan
◦ SNDP Yogam (1903) — Sree Narayana Guru

 

NOTE

 

• M.G. Ranade (Option 2): Its leading figure, but not its founder; he is called the Father of Indian Economics.

 

• Keshab Chandra Sen (Option 3): A leader of the Brahmo Samaj who inspired the founding of the Prarthana Samaj.

 

• Debendranath Tagore (Option 4): Led the Brahmo Samaj after Rammohan Roy and founded the Tattvabodhini Sabha.

question: Which gharana of Hindustani classical music is regarded as the oldest?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gwalior Gharana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Gwalior Gharana is regarded as the oldest gharana of Khayal singing in Hindustani classical music, and all the later gharanas are held to have grown out of it. (ग्वालियर घराना — सबसे प्राचीन घराना)

 

• It was founded by Nathan Peer Bakhsh and carried forward by his grandsons Haddu Khan and Hassu Khan. Its style is marked by simplicity, a plain and forceful voice, clear enunciation and an emphasis on the raga in its pure form.

 

• Distinguished exponents include Vishnu Digambar Paluskar, who founded the Gandharva Mahavidyalaya in 1901, and Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande, who systematised Hindustani music into ten thaats.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The principal gharanas of Hindustani vocal music and their characteristics:
◦ Gwalior — the oldest; simple and direct
◦ Agra — founded by Haji Sujan Khan; forceful, with an emphasis on dhrupad-like delivery
◦ Kirana — founded by Abdul Karim Khan and Abdul Wahid Khan; emphasis on slow tempo and the purity of individual notes; Bhimsen Joshi and Gangubai Hangal belonged to it
◦ Jaipur-Atrauli — founded by Alladiya Khan; complex and uncommon ragas; Kesarbai Kerkar and Mallikarjun Mansur
◦ Patiala — known for thumri and ornamentation; Bade Ghulam Ali Khan
◦ Rampur-Sahaswan and Bhendibazaar are the other well-known schools

 

• Tansen, one of Akbar's navratnas, is regarded as the fountainhead of the Hindustani tradition, and the Tansen Samaroh is held annually at Gwalior.

 

NOTE

 

• Agra (Option 2), Kirana (Option 3) and Patiala (Option 4) are all major gharanas, but each developed later than Gwalior.

question: What is the minimum distance from a reflecting surface required for a person to hear a distinct echo?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 17.2 metres.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The minimum distance from a reflecting surface required to hear a distinct echo is about 17.2 metres. (प्रतिध्वनि के लिए न्यूनतम दूरी — लगभग 17.2 मीटर)

 

• The calculation rests on the persistence of hearing. The sensation of a sound remains in the human ear for about 0.1 second, so the reflected sound must reach the ear at least 0.1 second after the original in order to be heard separately.
◦ Taking the speed of sound in air as 344 m/s:
◦ Distance travelled in 0.1 s = 344 × 0.1 = 34.4 m
◦ Since the sound must travel to the obstacle and back, the distance of the obstacle = 34.4 ÷ 2 = 17.2 m

 

• This is why echoes are heard in large empty halls, hills and wells, but not in a small room.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Reverberation is the persistence of sound produced by repeated reflection from the walls and ceiling of a large hall. Excessive reverberation blurs speech, which is why auditoriums are lined with sound-absorbing materials such as curtains, carpets, perforated boards and upholstered seats.

 

• Applications of the reflection of sound: SONAR, the stethoscope, the megaphone, ultrasound scanning, and the curved ceilings and sounding boards of concert halls.

 

• Sound is a longitudinal mechanical wave and cannot travel through a vacuum. Its speed is about 344 m/s in air, 1,500 m/s in water and 5,960 m/s in steel.

 

NOTE

 

• 10 metres (Option 1) and 25 metres (Option 3) do not follow from the standard values.

 

• 34.4 metres (Option 4) is the total distance travelled by the sound in 0.1 second, and is the commonest error — candidates forget to divide by two.

question: Which of the following is NOT a fibre crop?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sugarcane.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sugarcane is not a fibre crop. It is a cash crop grown for sugar, gur and khandsari, and it also yields molasses for the alcohol industry and bagasse for paper. (गन्ना — रेशेदार फसल नहीं)

 

• The four principal fibre crops of India are cotton, jute, hemp and natural silk. Of these the first three are grown in the soil, while silk is obtained from the cocoons of silkworms reared on mulberry leaves — a process called sericulture.

 

• Cotton requires black soil and high temperature; Gujarat and Maharashtra are the leading producers. Jute, the "golden fibre", grows in the well-drained alluvial soil of the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta; West Bengal is the largest producer.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Classification of crops in India:
◦ Food crops — rice, wheat, millets, maize, pulses
◦ Cash crops — sugarcane, oilseeds, tobacco
◦ Plantation crops — tea, coffee, rubber, coconut, spices; grown on estates and largely for the market
◦ Fibre crops — cotton, jute, hemp, silk
◦ Horticulture — fruits and vegetables

 

• Sugarcane is native to India, needs a hot and humid climate with 75-100 cm of rainfall, and is grown chiefly in Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and Karnataka. India is the second largest producer in the world after Brazil.

 

NOTE

 

• Cotton (Option 1): The most important fibre crop of India, used in the textile industry.

 

• Jute (Option 2): Used for making gunny bags, ropes, mats and carpets.

 

• Hemp (Option 3): Used for making rope, coarse cloth and paper.

question: Which of the following statements regarding the Balance of Payments (BoP) of a country is correct?
option_1: The current account records only the purchase and sale of financial assets.
option_2: The capital account records trade in goods and services.
option_3: The current account includes trade in goods and services and unilateral transfers.
option_4: The Balance of Payments of a country always shows a surplus.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The current account includes trade in goods and services and unilateral transfers.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Balance of Payments (BoP) is a systematic record of all economic transactions between the residents of a country and the rest of the world during a given period. It has two principal accounts: (भुगतान संतुलन — चालू खाता एवं पूँजी खाता)

 

• Current Account — records:
◦ Visible trade — the export and import of goods, whose net figure is the Balance of Trade
◦ Invisible trade — the export and import of services such as shipping, banking, insurance, tourism and software
◦ Unilateral transfers — remittances, gifts and grants, for which nothing is given in return

 

• Capital Account — records transactions in financial assets: foreign investment, loans, banking capital and changes in foreign exchange reserves.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Balance of Trade (BOT) = value of exports of goods − value of imports of goods. It is favourable (surplus) when exports exceed imports and unfavourable (deficit) when imports exceed exports. India has generally had a trade deficit, offset in part by remittances and software exports.

 

• The BoP as a whole always balances in the accounting sense, since any deficit on the current account must be financed by the capital account or by drawing down reserves — but it may show a deficit or surplus on either account.

 

• India faced a severe balance of payments crisis in 1991, when reserves fell to about two weeks' worth of imports, leading to the LPG reforms.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 reverses the two accounts — financial assets belong to the capital account.

 

• Option 2 likewise reverses them — trade in goods and services belongs to the current account.

 

• Option 4 is wrong; a country's BoP may show either a deficit or a surplus on its component accounts.

question: Who is the author of the book 'The Idea of India'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sunil Khilnani.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "The Idea of India" (1997) was written by Sunil Khilnani, and was published to mark the fiftieth anniversary of Indian independence. (द आइडिया ऑफ इंडिया — सुनील खिलनानी)

 

• The book examines how the idea of India as a modern democratic nation was conceived and given institutional form after 1947, with chapters on democracy, the city, the temples of the future (Nehru's phrase for dams and factories) and the working of the state.

 

• His other well-known work is "Incarnations: India in 50 Lives" (2016), a series of essays on figures from the Buddha to Dhirubhai Ambani.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Major works on modern India and their authors:
◦ "India After Gandhi" — Ramachandra Guha
◦ "India's Struggle for Independence" and "India Since Independence" — Bipan Chandra
◦ "The Argumentative Indian" and "Development as Freedom" — Amartya Sen
◦ "An Era of Darkness", "Why I Am a Hindu" and "The Great Indian Novel" — Shashi Tharoor
◦ "The Discovery of India" — Jawaharlal Nehru
◦ "The Rediscovery of India" — Meghnad Desai
◦ "Being Indian" — Pavan K. Varma
◦ "India Wins Freedom" — Maulana Abul Kalam Azad

 

NOTE

 

• Ramachandra Guha (Option 2): Author of "India After Gandhi" and "Gandhi Before India".

 

• Shashi Tharoor (Option 3): Author of "An Era of Darkness", on the economic impact of British rule.

 

• Amartya Sen (Option 4): Nobel laureate in economics, and author of "The Argumentative Indian".

question: Who won the JCB Prize for Literature in 2023 for the novel 'Fire Bird'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Perumal Murugan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Perumal Murugan won the JCB Prize for Literature in 2023 for his novel "Fire Bird", translated from the Tamil "Aalanda Patchi" by Janani Kannan. (जेसीबी पुरस्कार 2023 — पेरुमल मुरुगन, 'फायर बर्ड')

 

• The novel tells the story of Muthu, a man who must find new land and begin life afresh after his family's property is divided among the brothers.

 

• The prize carries ₹25 lakh for the author and an additional ₹10 lakh for the translator when the winning work is a translation.

 

• Perumal Murugan is a Tamil writer and professor, best known for "One Part Woman" (Madhorubagan).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The JCB Prize for Literature was instituted in 2018 and is awarded annually for a distinguished work of fiction by an Indian writer, including works in translation. Its winners include:
◦ 2018 — Benyamin, *Jasmine Days*
◦ 2019 — Madhuri Vijay, *The Far Field*

NOTE

question: The 'Rock Shelters of Bhimbetka', a UNESCO World Heritage Site, are located in which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Rock Shelters of Bhimbetka are situated in the Raisen district of Madhya Pradesh, in the foothills of the Vindhya range, about 45 km south of Bhopal. They were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2003. (भीमबेटका — मध्य प्रदेश)

 

• They contain prehistoric rock paintings, some of them dating back to the Mesolithic period and continuing into historical times. The paintings depict hunting, dancing, animals, horse and elephant riders and honey collection, and were executed chiefly in red and white.

 

• They were discovered in 1957-58 by the archaeologist Dr. Vishnu Shridhar Wakankar. The name is associated with Bhima of the Mahabharata.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Madhya Pradesh: the Khajuraho Group of Monuments (1986), the Buddhist Monuments at Sanchi (1989) and the Rock Shelters of Bhimbetka (2003).

 

• Sites in other states frequently asked: Champaner-Pavagadh and Rani ki Vav (Gujarat), Ajanta, Ellora and Elephanta (Maharashtra), Konark Sun Temple (Odisha), Hampi and Pattadakal (Karnataka), Great Living Chola Temples and Mahabalipuram (Tamil Nadu), and the Hill Forts of Rajasthan.

 

• India's first World Heritage Sites, inscribed in 1983, were the Agra Fort, the Taj Mahal, the Ajanta Caves and the Ellora Caves.

 

NOTE

 

• Karnataka (Option 1): Site of Hampi, Pattadakal and the Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas.

 

• Maharashtra (Option 2): Site of the Ajanta, Ellora and Elephanta caves.

 

• Odisha (Option 3): Site of the Konark Sun Temple.

question: The 'Moti Masjid' within the Agra Fort was built by which Mughal emperor?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shah Jahan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Moti Masjid (Pearl Mosque) within the Agra Fort was built by Shah Jahan between 1648 and 1654, entirely of white marble. It takes its name from the pearly lustre of the stone. (मोती मस्जिद, आगरा — शाहजहाँ)

 

• Shah Jahan's reign (1628-1658) is regarded as the golden age of Mughal architecture, marked by the extensive use of white marble in place of the red sandstone favoured by Akbar, and by pietra dura inlay.

 

• His principal buildings:
◦ The Taj Mahal at Agra, built for Mumtaz Mahal; chief architect Ustad Ahmad Lahauri
◦ The Red Fort and the Jama Masjid at Delhi, in his new capital Shahjahanabad
◦ The Diwan-i-Am and Diwan-i-Khas at Delhi, and the Peacock Throne
◦ The Moti Masjid at Agra and the Sheesh Mahal

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mughal builders and their works:
◦ Babur — gardens; the mosque at Panipat
◦ Humayun — Din Panah; his tomb at Delhi was built by his widow Hamida Banu Begum, the first garden tomb in India
◦ Akbar — Agra Fort, Fatehpur Sikri with its Buland Darwaza, and Lahore Fort
◦ Jahangir — chiefly gardens, such as Shalimar Bagh in Kashmir; the tomb of Itimad-ud-Daula at Agra was built by Nur Jahan for her father, and was the first Mughal structure entirely of white marble
◦ Aurangzeb — the Moti Masjid in the Red Fort, Delhi, and the Badshahi Mosque at Lahore; Bibi Ka Maqbara at Aurangabad was built by his son

 

NOTE

 

• Akbar (Option 1): Built the Agra Fort itself, in red sandstone, but not the Moti Masjid within it.

 

• Jahangir (Option 2): Better known for gardens and painting than for building.

 

• Aurangzeb (Option 4): Built a different Moti Masjid, inside the Red Fort at Delhi — the commonest confusion in this question.

question: Which of the following gases is chiefly responsible for the depletion of the ozone layer?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chlorofluorocarbons.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) are chiefly responsible for the depletion of the ozone layer. (क्लोरोफ्लोरोकार्बन — ओज़ोन क्षरण का मुख्य कारण)

 

• On reaching the stratosphere, CFC molecules are broken up by ultraviolet radiation and release chlorine atoms, each of which can destroy a very large number of ozone (O₃) molecules in a chain reaction before it is removed.

 

• CFCs were used as refrigerants, aerosol propellants and in the manufacture of foam. Their depletion of the ozone layer was first recognised in the 1970s, and the ozone hole over Antarctica was reported in 1985.

 

• The Montreal Protocol (1987) provides for the phasing out of ozone-depleting substances, and is regarded as the most successful environmental treaty ever concluded. 16 September is observed as the International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The distinction between the two great atmospheric problems is often tested:
◦ Ozone depletion — caused by CFCs, halons and carbon tetrachloride; occurs in the stratosphere; increases harmful ultraviolet radiation reaching the earth, causing skin cancer and cataract
◦ Global warming — caused by greenhouse gases — carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide, water vapour and CFCs — which trap the heat radiated back from the earth's surface

 

• The Kigali Amendment (2016) to the Montreal Protocol provides for the phase-down of hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), which do not deplete ozone but are potent greenhouse gases.

 

NOTE

 

• Carbon dioxide (Option 1) and Methane (Option 2): Major greenhouse gases responsible for global warming, but they do not deplete the ozone layer.

 

• Nitrogen (Option 4): Constitutes about 78% of the atmosphere and is chemically inert under ordinary conditions.

question: In the classification of Indian musical instruments, 'Tat Vadya' refers to which group?
option_4: Solid instruments struck against each other
solution_text:
The correct answer is Stringed instruments.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tat Vadya is the class of stringed instruments, known in the Western classification as chordophones. (तत् वाद्य — तंतु वाद्य)
◦ Examples: veena, sitar, sarod, tanpura, santoor, ektara, sarangi and violin

 

• The ancient Indian classification of musical instruments, set out in the Natyashastra of Bharata Muni, recognises four groups:
◦ Tat Vadya — stringed instruments (chordophones)
◦ Sushir Vadya — wind instruments (aerophones): flute, shehnai, nadaswaram, pungi, conch
◦ Avanaddha Vadya — instruments covered with a membrane, that is, drums (membranophones): tabla, mridangam, dholak, pakhawaj, khol
◦ Ghan Vadya — solid instruments that produce sound by being struck, without needing tuning (idiophones): manjira, jhanjh, ghatam, jaltarang, ghungroo

 

• Stringed instruments are further divided into those that are plucked (sitar, veena), bowed (sarangi, violin) and struck (santoor).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The veena is the oldest of Indian stringed instruments and is associated with Goddess Saraswati. The sitar and tabla are traditionally attributed to Amir Khusrau.

 

• Noted exponents: Ravi Shankar (sitar), Ali Akbar Khan (sarod), Bismillah Khan (shehnai), Hariprasad Chaurasia (flute), Shivkumar Sharma (santoor), Zakir Hussain (tabla) and M.S. Subbulakshmi (Carnatic vocal).

 

NOTE

 

• Wind instruments (Option 2): These are Sushir Vadya.

 

• Drums with a membrane (Option 3): These are Avanaddha Vadya.

 

• Solid instruments struck together (Option 4): These are Ghan Vadya.

question: Which cell organelle is known as the 'suicide bag' of the cell?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lysosome.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The lysosome is known as the "suicide bag" of the cell, a name given to it by its discoverer Christian de Duve. (लाइसोसोम — कोशिका की आत्मघाती थैली)

 

• It is a membrane-bound sac containing powerful hydrolytic (digestive) enzymes, and its functions are:
◦ To digest foreign material and worn-out cell organelles, keeping the cell clean
◦ To break down the cell itself when it is damaged or dying, by bursting and releasing its enzymes — hence the name

 

• Lysosomes are formed by the Golgi apparatus, and are found chiefly in animal cells.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Cell organelles and their popular names:
◦ Mitochondria — the powerhouse of the cell, where ATP is produced
◦ Ribosome — the protein factory
◦ Golgi apparatus — the dispatching or packaging unit
◦ Endoplasmic reticulum — the transport network; the rough ER bears ribosomes on its surface and makes proteins, while the smooth ER makes lipids
◦ Chloroplast — the kitchen of the plant cell
◦ Nucleus — the control centre, containing the DNA

 

• Organelles found only in plant cells: the cell wall (of cellulose), plastids and a large central vacuole. Centrioles are found only in animal cells.

 

NOTE

 

• Ribosome (Option 1): The site of protein synthesis; it has no membrane at all.

 

• Golgi apparatus (Option 3): Packages and dispatches materials, and forms the lysosomes.

 

• Vacuole (Option 4): A storage sac for water, food and waste; very large in plant cells.

question:
Which of the following are obtained as fractions from the fractional distillation of petroleum?

I. Petrol

II. Diesel
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Both statements are correct. Both petrol and diesel are obtained as fractions from the fractional distillation of petroleum. (पेट्रोल एवं डीजल — पेट्रोलियम के प्रभाजी आसवन से प्राप्त)

 

• Petroleum, or crude oil, is a mixture of hydrocarbons and cannot be used as such. It is separated in a fractionating column, in which the vapours rise and the various fractions condense at different heights according to their boiling points — the lighter fractions rising highest.

 

• The principal fractions, in order of increasing boiling point:
◦ Petroleum gas (LPG) — fuel for domestic and industrial use
◦ Petrol (gasoline) — fuel for light motor vehicles, and a solvent for dry cleaning
◦ Kerosene — fuel for stoves and lamps, and for jet aircraft
◦ Diesel — fuel for heavy motor vehicles and electric generators
◦ Lubricating oil — for lubrication
◦ Paraffin wax — for ointments, candles and vaseline
◦ Bitumen (asphalt) — for surfacing roads

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Petroleum is called "black gold" because of its value. It was formed from the remains of marine organisms buried under the sea bed over millions of years, and is therefore a fossil fuel and non-renewable.

 

• India's oil fields include Digboi, Naharkatiya and Moran (Assam), Ankleshwar and Kalol (Gujarat), Mumbai High (offshore), Barmer (Rajasthan) and the Krishna-Godavari basin.

 

• India imports well over 80% of its crude oil requirement. Digboi has India's oldest refinery, set up in 1901.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are incorrect, because both petrol and diesel are genuine fractions of petroleum.
